title: Duchy of Bohemia
capsule: The Duchy of Bohemia (České knížectví) coalesced as a distinct polity in 895, when Přemyslid dukes Spytihněv and Slavník swore allegiance to Carolingian king Arnulf at Regensburg, separating from the disintegrating Great Moravia. The duchy's formative century saw Wenceslaus I (r. 921–935) accept Saxon suzerainty, Boleslaus I (r. 935–972) expand Přemyslid territory into Moravia, Silesia, and Little Poland, and Boleslaus II co-found the Prague bishopric with Emperor Otto I in 973. In 1003 Bolesław I Chrobry of Poland seized Bohemia, briefly interrupting Přemyslid rule; the duchy was restored in 1004 and continued until its elevation to a kingdom in 1198 under Ottokar I, confirmed by the Golden Bull of Sicily in 1212.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of the Duchy of Bohemia is well attested through Frankish and Czech chronicles and preserved charters; border zones toward Moravia, Silesia, and Lusatia fluctuated and are less precisely bounded.
